clinician.final_diagnosis: Interstitial nephritis secondary to Asian giant hornet envenomation
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 42-year-old man was attacked by swarms of Asian giant hornets, sustaining 66 sting marks on exposed areas (face, head, neck, upper limb, upper thorax). He presented to the ED approximately 5 hours post-attack with difficulty breathing, headache, and numbness in both limbs. Initial vital signs showed sinus bradycardia (45-46/min) and blood pressure 136/90 mmHg. Laboratory findings on admission revealed leukocytosis (32.94×10^9/L), normal hemoglobin and platelets, and oliguria (200 ml/24h urine output). Urinalysis showed no proteinuria or hematuria. By day 3, serum creatinine had risen to 185 umol/L, indicating acute kidney injury, accompanied by marked elevation of liver enzymes (AST 1124 U/L, ALT 163.9 U/L), creatine kinase (5342.3 U/L), and cardiac markers (troponin I 1.092 ng/ml, CK-MB 577.0 U/L). By day 13, serum creatinine peaked at 534 umol/L with persistent oliguria (200 ml/24h), though cardiac markers had normalized. On day 17, kidney ultrasound demonstrated increased Doppler signal and thickened renal parenchyma (2.5 cm), consistent with renal edema. Kidney biopsy performed on day 17 confirmed interstitial nephritis, showing normal glomeruli, tubular epithelial cell vacuolization, and interstitial inflammation with eosinophil and lymphocyte infiltration. The patient was treated with methylprednisolone 32 mg/day orally. By day 31, renal function began recovering with urine output increasing to >2.8 L/day and serum creatinine decreasing to 159.3 umol/L, indicating the recovery phase of venom-induced acute interstitial nephritis.

Initial vital signs showed sinus bradycardia (45-46/min) and blood pressure 136/90 mmHg. Laboratory findings on admission revealed leukocytosis (32.94×10^9/L), normal hemoglobin and platelets, and oliguria (200 ml/24h urine output). Urinalysis showed no proteinuria or hematuria. By day 3, serum creatinine had risen to 185 umol/L, indicating acute kidney injury, accompanied by marked elevation of liver enzymes (AST 1124 U/L, ALT 163.9 U/L), creatine kinase (5342.3 U/L), and cardiac markers (troponin I 1.092 ng/ml, CK-MB 577.0 U/L). By day 13, serum creatinine peaked at 534 umol/L with persistent oliguria (200 ml/24h), though cardiac markers had normalized. On day 17, kidney ultrasound demonstrated increased Doppler signal and thickened renal parenchyma (2.5 cm), consistent with renal edema. Kidney biopsy performed on day 17 confirmed interstitial nephritis, showing normal glomeruli, tubular epithelial cell vacuolization, and interstitial inflammation with eosinophil and lymphocyte infiltration. The patient was treated with methylprednisolone 32 mg/day orally. By day 31, renal function began recovering with urine output increasing to >2.8 L/day and serum creatinine decreasing to 159.3 umol/L, indicating the recovery phase of venom-induced acute interstitial nephritis.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Massive Asian giant hornet envenomation with 66 sting marks on exposed areas
Acute kidney injury with serum creatinine elevation from normal baseline to 185 umol/L by day 3
Progressive deterioration of renal function with peak serum creatinine of 534 umol/L by day 13
Kidney ultrasound on day 17 showing increased Doppler signal and thickened renal parenchyma (2.5 cm), consistent with renal edema and inflammation
Kidney biopsy on day 17 confirming interstitial nephritis with normal glomeruli, tubular epithelial cell vacuolization, and interstitial inflammation with eosinophils and lymphocytes
Recovery phase with improved urine output (>2.8 L/day) and decreased serum creatinine (159.3 umol/L) by day 31
Treatment with methylprednisolone 32 mg/day orally during hospitalization
Multi-organ toxicity from hornet venom with markedly elevated transaminases, CK, and cardiac markers on day 3
Oliguria (200 ml/24h) on day 1 and persistent through day 13, with recovery by day 31

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Kidney biopsy showed normal glomeruli with no glomerular involvement; interstitial inflammation with eosinophils and lymphocytes is the primary pathology

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.alternative: Acute tubular necrosis (ATN) as primary diagnosis
ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: While tubular epithelial cell vacuolization was present, the dominant histological finding was interstitial inflammation with eosinophil and lymphocyte infiltration, characteristic of interstitial nephritis rather than ATN

Although CK was markedly elevated (5342.3 U/L), the kidney biopsy findings of interstitial inflammation with eosinophils and lymphocytes are more consistent with drug/toxin-induced interstitial nephritis than rhabdomyolysis-induced ATN
